title: Reserve bucket pricing & HC allocation experiments
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a set of small-batch experiments combining (A) a short-term reserve bucket for hiring flex ("floating headcount"), and (B) three pricing pivot points to evaluate sensitivity on ARR, gross margin, and runway. Goal is to produce a quick decision rubric for Q2 hiring freezes/deferrals and for a targeted price test on a subset of Hosted API customers.

High-level framing:
- We keep an explicit 6-month 'reserve bucket' of uncommitted HC budget (FTEs budgeted but not filled) so the company can flex between hiring (to meet demand) and pause (to protect runway).
- Pair reserve bucket decisions with small price tests (covering -8% / base / +18% pivot) to understand elasticity on usage and conversion for self-serve and sales-assisted cohorts.
- Output: a matrix showing monthly burn delta, 12-month ARR delta, and probability-weighted runway impact under three demand sensitivities.

Key assumptions (editable cells):
- Average fully-loaded cost per new hire by function (annual): Eng = $260k, ML Eng = $295k, SRE = $250k, Sales AE = $180k, CS AM = $150k, Other = $120k.
- Hiring lead time: 6 weeks for Sales/CS, 10 weeks for Eng/ML/SRE. Ramp to full productivity: 3 months for revenue-facing (sales/cs), 6 months for eng/ml/sre for capacity impact.
- Baseline ARR (weighted) at start of Q1 2026: $78.4M. Monthly recurring revenue = ARR/12.
- Baseline gross margin on hosted usage and dedicated contracts: 62% (post-infra, pre-opex).
- Elasticity assumptions for price test cohorts: Conservative (inelastic) = -5% usage per +10% price; Base = -10% per +10%; Aggressive (elastic) = -18% per +10%. These apply asymmetrically for price decreases/increases.
- Test cohorts size: Self-serve pilot = 8% of usage; Sales-assisted pilot = 4% of usage; remainder excluded.

Reserve bucket design (6-month horizon):
- Reserve bucket = 18 FTEs equivalent (budgeted but unfilled). Allocation plan (initial draft): Eng 8, ML Eng 2, SRE 2, Sales 3, CS 3.
- Cost if fully filled (annualized): ~ $3.6M run-rate. Monthly burn if filled = $300k.
- Decision triggers: Fill if 3-month trailing usage growth > 6% and utilization SLOs degrade (p99 latency > target) or committed pipeline MRR > $2.2M over baseline. Defer if 3-month trailing usage growth < 1% or ARR churn > 0.9% MRR.

Pricing pivot scenarios (applied to pilot cohorts only):
- Down Tier (P-8): price change -8% (timeout: 8 weeks), expected usage lift by elasticity assumptions above.
- Base (P0): no price change.
- Up Tier (P+18): price change +18% (timeout: 8 weeks), expected usage drop per elasticity.

Sensitivity matrix (single-month snapshot, illustrative):
Columns: Scenario | Price Delta | Pilot Usage Delta | Monthly Rev Delta (pilot) | Monthly Gross Margin Delta | Monthly Cash Burn Impact | HC Fill Recommendation
- Conservative down: P-8 | -8% | +4% usage | -$210k | -$80k | negative (worse cash) -> hold reserve
- Conservative up: P+18 | +18% | -9% usage | +$380k | +$150k | positive -> consider deferring 3 hires (sales/CS)
- Base: P0 | 0% | 0% | $0 | $0 | neutral -> stagger hiring (fill 4/18)
- Aggressive down: P-8 | -8% | +14% usage | -$730k | -$280k | worse cash -> freeze fills, consider short-term credits instead
- Aggressive up: P+18 | +18% | -32% usage | +$1.1M | +$420k | materially positive -> consider gradual hiring and targeted sales comp re-allocation

12-month projection sensitivity (summary numbers, probability-weighted):
- Upside (P+18, conservative elasticity): incremental ARR +$4.6M, incremental gross margin +$1.9M, runway +0.9 months (if paired with 50% reserve deferral).
- Base: incremental ARR $0, runway neutral (0 months).
- Downside (P-8, aggressive elasticity): ARR -$8.3M, gross margin -$3.2M, runway -1.8 months (if reserve filled fully).

Headcount phasing plan (6 quarters view, suggested):
- Q1: Hold 12/18 reserve (only hire critical replacements) -> net hires: +6 (splits: Eng 3, Sales 1, CS 1, SRE 1).
- Q2: Based on P+18 pilot results, either proceed to fill additional 6 or hold.
- Q3: Re-evaluate; aim to have reserve reduced to 6 if demand strong.

Quick decision rubric (for CFO + GTM lead + Eng VP):
- If pilot P+18 yields >12% revenue net uplift at pilot scale AND churn stable (<0.9% MRR), convert reserve to targeted hiring (priority: Sales then Eng then SRE).
- If pilot P-8 shows net ARR decline >5% or gross margin erosion >2ppt, suspend all non-critical requisitions immediately and run a 30-day re-price & retention playbook.
- If usage growth triggers capacity SLO degradation, authorize emergency fill but only from reserve and only for Eng/SRE; cap at 4 hires in a 60-day window.

Risks & unknowns (for alignment):
- Elasticity may differ materially between self-serve token usage and enterprise committed usage. Enterprise customers likely have stickier consumption and different negotiation behavior.
- Ramp assumptions for Eng/ML on capacity improvements are uncertain; we need short A/B telemetry: p99 latency and batch utilization per model.
- Pilot measurement windows must be long enough to capture billing rhythm (30–60 days) and factor in seasonality.

Next steps (owner: Asha):
1) Finalize pilot cohorts with product (who gets P+18) and legal (contract amendments for pilot).
2) Provision a 6-week analytics slice: cohort usage, churn, new ARR, and SLOs. (Owner: Riley)
3) Finance to prepare a short-term hiring hold memo with guardrails for People Ops (Owner: Daniel).
4) Re-run sensitivity with live pilot numbers 6 weeks post-launch and circulate updated decision memo.

Appendix (quick calculation cells):
- Example monthly impact calc for pilot (simplified): Pilot MRR start = $1.2M; price +18% -> new price * usage delta (-12% under base elasticity) = net +4.9% -> delta MRR ~ +$59k/month in pilot; scaling to full base cohort multiplies accordingly.
- Break-even hire calculus: 1 Sales AE (FL cost ~$15k/month) needs to close incremental ARR > $180k ARR (annualized) in 12 months to pay back purely on gross margin contribution.

Notes: This is an active, editable sheet. Cells marked in bold in the live version are the knobs (per-hire cost, cohort size, elasticity). Keep pilot narrow and instrumented.

Contact: Asha.Patel@redwood.ai for questions or if you want to change the reserve allocation split.
